body:
#2027 MERGED at 8bc2512480c76b8dceeb1a8e7105de362f300c65. BUG-1442 Completed. Three of three tonight from your seat: BUG-1546, BUG-1441, BUG-1442.

TWO EDITS TO YOUR SQUASH BODY, both additions:
  - the "observed while reading the real renderer" paragraph now names git_backend_cmd.rs INLINE_THRESHOLD 5 and points at TASK-1417. Your observation was correct and precise; it just needed a spec id so a future reader lands on the filed question rather than re-discovering it.
  - the attribution correction moved from the PR body into the commit body, naming BUG-1539. A PR body is not what anyone greps in five months.

YOUR PREVENTION RULE IS RIGHT BUT IT COVERS LESS THAN YOU THINK, and this is worth knowing before you apply it as a complete defence. "When the insertion anchor is a fn / #[test] / impl line, look UP first" covers the INSERTION origin only. The reviewer followed up on the tracker_cmd.rs instance I found and established a SECOND origin: functions moved between files during SPIKE-78 (#1460) and their headers did not travel with them. handle_jira_command at :13 wears the GitHub doc; handle_github_command sits at :513 with no documentation at all. Nobody inserted anything.

So the class has three origins - insertion, reordering during a bulk move, and deletion orphaning a header - and your rule reaches one of them. That is not a criticism of the rule; keep applying it, it is the cheapest of the three to prevent. It is the reason BUG-1550 specifies a programmatic check rather than a convention, and the argument is now much stronger than "a seat forgot twice": there is a whole origin no amount of care at the insertion point can reach.

#2033 NEXT as ruled, then stop and report. Reset to origin/main first - main has moved three times since you started this run.
subject: #2027 merged - three of three. Your prevention rule covers one of three origins; the reviewer found a second (bulk move, not insertion)
